subject: When should PC scores be mulitplied by -1?

messages.author: 96a78639336ed702
messages.subject: When should PC scores be mulitplied by -1?
parts:
Hi,

In Sherratt's paper "A new, three-dimensional geometric morphometric approach to assess egg shape", to plot PCA of PC1 vs PC2, the authors performed pca through PCA <- plotTangentSpace(egg.gpa.surfs$coords, groups= species, warpgrids = F). The authors then multiplied PC scores by -1 (PCA$pc.scores[,1] <- PCA$pc.scores[,1] * -1) and explained "Original alphabetical order of species gave PC1 the other way around, so swap these here for ease of reference". I do not fully understand what this means and would like to know when is it necessary to multiply pc scores by -1.

Another question is that the author used refmesh <- warpRefMesh(mesh, meshcoords[,,1], ref, color="#F0EAD6", centered=T) to warp a mesh close to the mean shape to ref (the mean shape). Before this step, when the mesh object was loaded (mesh <- file2mesh("PLY/Colluricincia_harmonica_E6328_Egg2.ply")), the authors said "need to rotate egg" and used mesh <- pcAlign(mesh) to "align by principal axes". My second question is why is it necessary to align by prinicpal axes before warping? What if not?

Thank you.

Regards,
Lv Xiao

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] When should PC scores be mulitplied by -1?
parts:
None of these operations are "necessary", or have any influence to the data. Although I do not know the details of the authors´decisions, I assume they were used for visualization purposes.

In the case of PC axes, their orientation is arbitrary, so in some cases it becomes more intuitive to invert their direction (e.g. if "large" individuals based on some size measure appear with negative PC scores due to a negative loading of size-related variables that axis).

As for the meshes, this is done to put the shape plots (in this case the meshes) in a specific direction for visualization. Due to how the data where digitized, the plots might end up having e.g. an egg oriented diagonally, and this operations just rotates the picture a bit so the egg has its long axis horizontal. Again, no effect on the data.

Hope this helps,

Antigoni
